numerical_failure.observed_behavior: The default tanh JVP rule computes (g + g * ans) * (1 - ans), which is not bit-for-bit symmetric under x -> -x when g != 1, so jvp(-x) and grad(-x) can differ from jvp(x) and grad(x) by floating-point rounding.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The default tanh JVP rule should compute g * ((1 + ans) * (1 - ans)), so that jvp(-x) == jvp(x) and grad(-x) == grad(x) bit-for-bit.

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: x in [0.1, 8.9] for the symmetry test (linspace of 100 points, float32)
category_specific_evidence: The default tanh JVP rule changed from (g + g * ans) * (1 - ans) to g * ((1 + ans) * (1 - ans)) to avoid premature rounding when g != 1 and to guarantee bit-for-bit symmetry jvp(-x) == jvp(x) and grad(-x) == grad(x).

The new test testTanhGradSymmetry in tests/lax_test.py uses x = linspace(0.1, 8.9, 100) in float32, g filled with 1.3, and checks jvp and grad symmetry with assertArraysEqual (exact equality, not a tolerance).
The test also checks grad of jnp.float32(1.3) * lax.tanh(z) under vmap for x and -x with exact equality.
tests/xla_metadata_test.py changed the expected HLO op for tanh(x) from "add" to "multiply" as a consequence of the JVP rewrite.
reproduction_risks: The passages give no separate tolerance: the symmetry check is exact bitwise equality, so any tolerance-based comparison would not reproduce the claimed property.
The passages do not state a precision/dtype dependence beyond float32 in the test; behavior in other dtypes is not described.
The magnitude regime where the asymmetry actually manifests is not stated; the test range 0.1 to 8.9 is only the test input range.
Tolerance at which correct and incorrect answers separate is not stated in any passage.
